summary: The Walking Dead entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: The Walking Dead: Season One
entries.definitive_edition: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series on Windows

primary.version: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series
primary.why: The Definitive Series is the modern complete route for Telltale's Walking Dead saga and includes Season One plus 400 Days and later seasons. For this entry, use it to play Season One and 400 Days, with PC as the best capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Use The Telltale Definitive Series on Windows and play Season One plus 400 Days for this entry. Use the original standalone only if preserving original 2012 presentation/UI.

all_releases.platform: Original Windows / macOS / console / mobile release family
all_releases.reason: skip: historical route, but Definitive Series is the current complete package.

all_releases.platform: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series on Windows / consoles
all_releases.fidelity: Modern collection route including Season One, 400 Days, and later series content.
all_releases.reason: primary: current complete route, with Windows preferred for capture.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Definitive Series is the complete modern route, but original releases preserve the 2012 episodic presentation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Keep Season One distinct from later seasons inside the Definitive Series package. Record whether 400 Days is included in this entry's run.

entries.title: The Walking Dead: Season Two
entries.definitive_edition: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High settings at native resolution, Graphic Black disabled for original-style art.

primary.version: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series
primary.why: The Definitive Series contains all four seasons, 400 Days, and Michonne in one continuity-preserving package, while adding dynamic lighting, performance/lip-sync/UI fixes, and bonus material. On PC it has the highest settings ceiling and keeps the complete Season Two story.
primary.how_to_play: Play Season One and 400 Days first so their choices import into Season Two. In the Definitive Menu, use High graphics and disable Graphic Black for Season Two every time the collection starts if you want the original art direction; the option defaults back on.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original release presentation without the collection's lighting, lip-sync, and UI revisions.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the original PC season only if a Definitive Series visual regression matters to the run.
secondary.why: It is the clean preservation fallback for exact original rendering, but it lacks the collection's fixes and unified extras.

all_releases.fidelity: Original art, lighting, menus, and episode builds.
all_releases.reason: secondary preservation fallback; Definitive Series otherwise carries the full season and improvements.

all_releases.platform: PS3 / Xbox 360 / PS Vita / iOS / Android
all_releases.fidelity: Contemporary console, handheld, and mobile ports.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower rendering/input ceiling and no verified story content absent from PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Later console ports of the standalone season.
all_releases.reason: skip: convenient disc-era fallback, but superseded by the complete collection.

all_releases.fidelity: Dynamic lighting, gameplay/UI/lip-sync improvements, optional Graphic Black, and collection-wide bonuses.
all_releases.reason: primary: complete unified package; PC provides the highest settings ceiling.
skip: portability does not outweigh the PC collection's complete continuity and improvements.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The collection is more complete and technically improved, but its Graphic Black treatment was auto-generated for earlier seasons and can look too dark. Because it is optional, disable it for Season Two and keep the rest of the Definitive Series advantages.

entries.remaster_caveats: Graphic Black was retrofitted onto Season Two, defaults to enabled on every startup, and can make non-Final-Season episodes excessively dark, especially at Low settings. Disable it for the original Season Two look; the collection also changes lighting, lip sync, and parts of the UI.
